references.text: John the Baptist later explains that the entire purpose of his water baptism was to reveal Christ to Israel: "So that he might be revealed to Israel, I came baptizing with water." Furthermore, he describes the contrast between his water baptism and Jesus' baptism with the Holy Spirit ([ref:Joh 1:31-33|John 1:31-33]).

In Matthew's account, John says similar words about baptizing with water, but that the one coming after him is more powerful and will baptize with the Holy Spirit and fire ([ref:Matt 3:11|Matthew 3:11]).
In Mark's account, John says that the one coming after him is stronger, and that he himself baptizes with water, while the coming one will baptize with the Holy Spirit ([ref:Mark 1:7-8|Mark 1:7-8]).
Luke also records John's testimony that he baptizes with water, but that a more powerful one than him is coming, who will baptize with the Holy Spirit and fire ([ref:Luk 3:16|Luke 3:16]).
Jesus himself refers back to John's water baptism and the contrast with the baptism of the Spirit: "John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit" ([ref:Apg 1:5|Acts 1:5]).

John's words that "in your midst stands one whom you do not know" reflect what was already said in the prologue: Jesus was in the world, but the world did not know him, and his own people did not receive him ([ref:Joh 1:10-11|John 1:10-11]).

The prophecy in Malachi that the Lord will suddenly come to his temple – "the Lord whom you seek" – is reflected in John's words that there stands among them one they do not know ([ref:Mal 3:1|Malachi 3:1]).
The next verse continues John's testimony about the one who comes after, for whom he is not worthy to untie the sandal strap ([ref:Joh 1:27|John 1:27]).
Paul explains that John baptized with a baptism of repentance and told the people to believe in the one coming after – that is, Jesus Christ ([ref:Apg 19:4|Acts 19:4]).
